title: Figure 3 · IBL 3D localization
caption:
Figure 3. IBL 3D localization. Main LFPformer results use the frozen 75k MaskPred + ManipDistc encoder (ep53); panel c additionally includes two frozen no-LFP-pretraining encoder controls. The LFP-only transformer is direct-XYZ ProbeSeq (decompose=False): known on-probe geometry, depth encoding, cross-channel attention and a Gaussian uncertainty head are retained, without a learned rigid pose branch. LFPformer is our method; TF = transformer readout, linear = linear readout, manip. = micromanipulator coordinates. All three transformer pretraining rows average decoder seeds 1-7 and 42. All errors are left-hemisphere-folded 3D RMSE in micrometers; ↓ next to an axis or colour-bar label means lower is better. 

(a) Regional Kabsch RMSE on sagittal (ML 4125), coronal (AP 7500) and axial (DV 3500) Allen CCF slices. As in c, every probe has equal weight: for each probe with channels in a region, the RMSE over its channels there (all of the region's channels, not just those within the displayed slice), then the mean over those probes; computed per seed and then averaged. Colours span 400-3000 micrometers; values outside take the end colours. The five models share 38,147 channels in the strict 309-region set. Grey denotes regions outside the scored set.

(b) Per-channel post-Kabsch 3D RMSE by Allen major brain region (plus fiber tracts and ventricles), on the channels of panel a. Violins show every channel's error (seed-averaged for LFPformer); bars mark the median; dots, joined per model, give the RMSE over the brain region's channels, every channel weighted equally (per seed, then averaged). Grey bars above the panel give each brain region's number of channels (k = thousand); the y axis is cut at 6000 micrometers.

(c) Per-probe post-Kabsch 3D RMSE. Each point is the mean of the per-probe RMSE values and whiskers show one sample standard deviation across probes (not a standard error, bootstrap interval or decoder-seed spread); numbers give mean ± SD. For LFPformer each probe's RMSE is first averaged over decoder seeds 1-7 and 42. Every probe has equal weight regardless of its channel count; panels a and d-h use the same per-probe weighting. Every row uses the same 118 test probes, those with micromanipulator coordinates: IBL's only micromanipulator trajectory for the 119th test probe (insertion b73ef9cf, subject SWC_042) records zero depth, so no insertion axis exists, and histology or planned trajectories were not substituted. That probe is omitted from the LFP-only rows in this panel only; panels a, b, and d-h use all 119 probes. Rows within each group are sorted by RMSE. LFPformer (TF) and the two wav2vec2 (TF) rows form the matched transformer encoder pretraining ablation. The LFPformer (TF) row freezes the 75k MaskPred + ManipDistc ep53 encoder. The matched wav2vec2 audio-pretrained control freezes the exact wav2vec2-base step-0 initialization with no LFP pretraining; the wav2vec2 random-init control freezes the same architecture with neither audio nor LFP pretraining. Both controls use the same direct-XYZ Gaussian transformer recipe, decoder seeds, 493,744 retained chunks and 118 probes as the LFPformer (TF) row. The upper group adds the three micromanipulator insertion coordinates to the frozen embeddings, read out by a linear head or a direct-XYZ transformer, and shows the micromanipulator coordinates alone. The transformer fusion readout was trained with six held-out validation subjects and a constant learning rate, whereas the LFP-only transformer below uses the earlier recipe (held-out windows, cosine schedule), so the difference between those two rows also reflects the training recipe. No significance markers are shown: the earlier paired probe-bootstrap tests were computed on the channel-weighted aggregate, a different statistic.

(d) RAW chunk predictions, inverse-variance channel pooling, and unweighted per-probe Kabsch on the pooled channels. Kabsch fits known probe geometry to predictions without true brain coordinates. Models lacking uncertainty use equal-weight pooling; ViT/AnyNet use their saved Gaussian-weighted consensus. RAW metrics weight chunks, while pooled/Kabsch metrics weight channels. Clouds show seed 1 for LFPformer and the single baseline run; annotations give the per-probe RMSE mean ± SD across probes, as in c (seed-averaged per probe for LFPformer). Point colours show each point's 3D RMSE (for a single point, its 3D distance from the true position), clipped at 3500 micrometers.

(e-h) Per-region, per-subject, per-probe and per-laboratory Kabsch RMSE for LFPformer (linear) versus ViT and AnyNet. As in c, every probe has equal weight: each group's value is the mean of the per-probe RMSE over the probes in that group (for regions, each probe's RMSE over its channels in the region). These preserve the per-channel decoder comparison; they do not use the transformer.

Direct-XYZ ProbeSeq per-probe RMSE, mean ± SD across probes: raw 1045.8 ± 578.2, pooled 1025.3 ± 561.8, kabsch 1009.7 ± 565.4 micrometers (119 probes).

title: Figure 4 · Cross-dataset brain-region classification
caption: Figure 4. Cross-dataset brain-region classification. (a) Balanced accuracy on Allen, IBL and NeuroNexus recordings. On every dataset, MaskPred + ChanDistc and MaskPred + ManipDistc are shown under full fine-tuning and frozen-encoder transfer; zero-shot transfer is additionally shown for NeuroNexus and for both Allen objective transfers. Allen zero-shot applies the IBL-trained Gaussian coordinate model without Allen fitting; IBL zero-shot is not defined in this comparison. Every IBL balanced-accuracy method is evaluated at physical-channel resolution: raw window-level XYZ predictions are inverse-variance pooled when uncertainty is available (ordinary means otherwise), followed by an unweighted per-probe Kabsch fit and the shared strict 309-class atlas lookup; out-of-atlas predictions count as errors. The frozen IBL results use matched eight-seed Gaussian ProbeSeq Transformer decoders (L4/d256/h8). These frozen balanced-accuracy values are the same stored endpoints used by Supplementary Fig. 5b. Allen uses the original Gaussian consensus/depth-line protocol so the surviving ChanDistc anchors and all baselines remain protocol-matched. The four Allen fine-tuned and frozen entries use the same Gaussian XYZ MLP decoder architecture (768-512-256-128 with separate mean and log-variance heads) and Gaussian NLL; full FT updates encoder and decoder, whereas frozen updates only the decoder. Native ManipDistc pretraining requires micromanipulator trajectories and is therefore available only on IBL; dagger-marked Allen ManipDistc entries transfer the IBL-pretrained encoder to an Allen-trained decoder; dagger-marked Allen ZS entries transfer each IBL-trained encoder and decoder without Allen fitting. Allen evaluates 116 classes. Error bars are sample SD over five folds (Allen and IBL baselines/full-FT), eight decoder seeds (frozen IBL), or seven held-out sessions (NeuroNexus). Bars are grouped into LFPformer (ChanDistc), LFPformer (ManipDistc) and baselines; dotted horizontal lines denote balanced-accuracy chance. ↑ / ↓ next to an axis label means higher / lower is better. (b) Corresponding macro-averaged one-vs-rest ROC curves; the dashed diagonal denotes chance. The number in each panel is the highest macro AUC among the LFPformer variants, in that variant's colour. Insets show each dataset's anatomical coverage on a sagittal section (1.5 mm first-hit slab of the 25 micrometer Allen CCF; covered regions in their Allen colours, all others grey), one hemisphere per dataset: Allen recordings lie in the right hemisphere; IBL coordinates are folded to the left hemisphere (right-hemisphere probes mirrored); NeuroNexus provides region labels only (hemisphere not recorded) and is drawn on the left. The schematic beside each inset shows one shank tip with recording sites to scale: Neuropixels 1.0 for Allen and IBL (staggered sites at 11, 27, 43 and 59 micrometers across, 20 micrometer rows) and the NeuroNexus probe (two aligned columns 15 micrometers apart, 20 micrometer pitch; shank outline schematic). The legends under a (bars) and b (curves) list the same models; LFPformer (ChanDistc) and LFPformer (ManipDistc) are pretrained with MaskPred + ChanDistc and MaskPred + ManipDistc; fine-tuned = full fine-tuning; PSD = power spectral density. Allen zero-shot ROC uses continuous coordinate scores. The historical NeuroNexus zero-shot artifacts retain hard best-k predictions but not confidence scores, so those ROC curves use one-hot hard-decision scores. Exact values, protocols, and checkpoint sources are recorded in fig4_final_numbers.json. Text sizes match the printed sizes of Supplementary Fig. 6 and Fig. 3.

title: Figure 5 · Coordinates emerge during pretraining
caption: Base-model training progression with frozen linear Gaussian readouts. Top: the shared audio-pretrained facebook/wav2vec2-base initialization at zero LFP-pretraining steps, shown once as AP, DV and ML coordinate plots. Middle: 5k steps (2.56M sample presentations). Bottom: 115k steps (58.88M sample presentations). Middle and bottom columns show MaskPred, +ChanDistc, +ManipDistc and +CCFDistc (atlas-supervised oracle). All nine checkpoint/readout cells use decoder seed 1, the same 500,000 test windows and 39,615 channels, per-axis inverse-variance pooling and left/right folding. No prediction or ground-truth mean is subtracted. AP and DV are original atlas coordinates; ML is folded distance from the Allen midline. Clouds precede per-probe Kabsch alignment. Insets report Pearson r, R² and axis-wise RMSE from uncentred coordinates. Corresponding coordinates use identical axis limits at all stages. Colours denote ground-truth Allen major brain regions; dashed lines denote identity.

title: Figure 6 · Data, model-size and compute scaling
caption:
Figure 6. Data, model-size and compute scaling. Colours denote the four pretraining objectives; thin dashed lines denote the base encoder (95.1M parameters) and bold solid lines the large encoder (317.5M parameters). The y axis is the Kabsch-aligned 3D RMSE in every panel (↓ lower is better). The x axes of a and c are logarithmic. (a) RMSE of a frozen linear readout versus the cumulative number of pretraining chunks (one chunk = one 3-s single-channel LFP window; optimization step × 512 chunks), for all 154 currently validated checkpoint records. This rendering is provisional: Large MaskPred is complete through step 100,000 (51.2 million chunks), while the recovered genuine Large ChanDistc curve currently ends at step 50,000 (25.6 million chunks) and is continuing toward the matched step-100,000 endpoint. (b) Decoder parameters, for both encoder sizes, at an exactly matched data budget: every point uses the step-35,000 checkpoint (17.92 million chunks), the largest checkpoint shared by every objective and both encoder sizes. Each x position is one readout, ordered by its trainable parameter count; the grey bars at the top of the panel give that count (log scale) and the tick label gives the architecture (Linear, the frozen linear readout; MLP-k, a per-channel MLP with k hidden layers; TF L×d, a probe-level Transformer with L blocks of width d). Parameter counts are for the base encoder's 768-dimensional input; the large encoder's 1024-dimensional input adds 1.5k–65.5k parameters per readout. All non-linear readouts are direct-XYZ Gaussian decoders. Each point is one value per readout: for the decoders, the mean over decoder seeds 1–7 and 42 (seed spread not shown); for the linear readout, its checkpoint value as in panel a. Base and large points are offset horizontally within each slot for visibility, and lines connect the readouts of one objective and encoder size. (c) RMSE of the frozen linear readout versus nominal pretraining compute through the final available CCFDistc checkpoint (6.54 × 10^18 FLOPs; 131 checkpoint records). Later checkpoints beyond that matched compute cutoff are excluded.

All readouts use per-axis inverse-variance channel pooling followed by an unweighted per-probe Kabsch fit and left-hemisphere-folded scoring. Kabsch uses known probe geometry and predicted coordinates, not true brain coordinates, in the fit. Pretraining compute is the nominal 6NFBS estimate and does not include geometric-loss, evaluation, or restart overhead. Decoder parameter counts are measured for each encoder input width and do not reuse the older pose-head counts.

title: Supplementary Fig. 7a · Per region, subject, probe and lab
caption: Supplementary Figure 7a. Localization error per region, subject, probe and lab. Each panel plots the 3D RMSE of LFPformer (ManipDistc) (x axis) against one comparator (y axis; rows: MaskPred only, ChanDistc only, CCFDistc only, ViT, AnyNet and LFPformer (ChanDistc)) for every Allen fine region (n = 309), subject (34), probe (119) and lab (12) of the IBL test set; lower is better, and x and y share one range per column. Points in the grey area lie above the diagonal, where LFPformer (ManipDistc) has the lower error; the number in each panel counts these groups (per region: MaskPred only 268/309, ChanDistc only 277/309, CCFDistc only 272/309, ViT 258/309, AnyNet 253/309, LFPformer (ChanDistc) 172/309). Errors follow the Fig. 3e–h protocol: window predictions are pooled per channel with inverse-variance weights, the probe's known channel geometry is rigidly fitted to them per probe (Kabsch; no ground-truth coordinates are used), and the result is folded to the left hemisphere; within each group, each probe's channel RMSE is computed and probes are averaged with equal weight. ViT and AnyNet are the Fig. 3 baselines. Dot colours: regions take their Allen CCF colour; each lab has one colour, each subject a shade of its lab's colour, and each probe its subject's colour. The legends list the Allen divisions, subjects, labs and probes (first eight characters of the IBL probe ID; the subject and lab of every probe are given in fig7_probes.csv). LFPformer (X) denotes the MaskPred + X encoder with the direct-XYZ Gaussian Transformer readout, averaged over decoder seeds 1–7 and 42; single-objective encoders (X only) use per-channel Gaussian decoders. All encoders are pretrained on the IBL 75k set. Because the single-objective encoders and the LFPformer systems use different readouts, the comparison is between complete systems and does not isolate the pretraining objective.

title: Supplementary Fig. 7b · Depth-5 confusion matrices
caption: Supplementary Figure 7b. Depth-5 region classification from predicted coordinates. Confusion matrices for the five LFP systems (MaskPred only, ChanDistc only, CCFDistc only, LFPformer (ChanDistc) and LFPformer (ManipDistc)). Predicted 3D coordinates are assigned to Allen depth-5 regions; six regions are shown and all others are pooled as Other. Cells give the percentage of each true region assigned to each predicted region (row-normalised; for the LFPformer systems, counts are averaged over decoder seeds before normalising; numbers are printed for cells ≥ 10%). Titles give balanced accuracy (higher is better; mean ± SD over seeds for the LFPformer systems). Balanced accuracy is 0.563 ± 0.021 for LFPformer (ChanDistc) and 0.559 ± 0.025 for LFPformer (ManipDistc). Top-1 accuracies: MaskPred only 0.353; ChanDistc only 0.332; CCFDistc only 0.323; LFPformer (ChanDistc) 0.669 ± 0.018; LFPformer (ManipDistc) 0.676 ± 0.015. All systems are scored on the same 362,314 test windows that lie in the 309 canonical fine regions. For every system the probe's known channel geometry is rigidly fitted per probe to the predictions (Kabsch; no ground-truth coordinates), using the per-window Gaussian outputs for the single-objective encoders and inverse-variance channel-pooled outputs for the LFPformer systems; coordinates are folded to the left hemisphere about ML = 5,700 µm. LFPformer (X) denotes the MaskPred + X encoder with the direct-XYZ Gaussian Transformer readout, averaged over decoder seeds 1–7 and 42; single-objective encoders (X only) use per-channel Gaussian decoders. All encoders are pretrained on the IBL 75k set. Because the single-objective encoders and the LFPformer systems use different readouts, the comparison is between complete systems and does not isolate the pretraining objective.

title: Supplementary Fig. 11 · LFPformer readouts with the micromanipulator
caption: Supplementary Figure 11. LFPformer readouts that combine LFP with the micromanipulator record. (a) An example IBL test probe on a coronal section (AP 7.5 mm; faded Allen CCF colours), with its logged micromanipulator track m (dashed, entry to tip) and its histology track y (solid; the training target), and four of its 3-s single-channel LFP chunks at increasing depth, coloured and labelled by their histology region in Allen CCF colours: VISrl, rostrolateral visual area (layer 2/3); CA1, hippocampal field CA1; LGd, dorsal part of the lateral geniculate nucleus (thalamus); ZI, zona incerta. The CA1 chunk (thicker line) is followed into b. Every chunk is embedded by the frozen LFPformer encoder (768 dimensions; strips show 24 of them, grey = low, magenta = high). (b) Linear readout, one chunk at a time: each chunk's embedding is concatenated with its channel's micromanipulator coordinates m (AP, DV, ML in mm) and mapped to a Gaussian mean and variance of the channel's 3D position (771 → 6); the stacked rows indicate that the same mapping is applied separately to every chunk. Transformer readout, many chunks of a probe at once: each chunk becomes one token [embedding | m] (together with its channel's position on the probe), and all of a probe's chunks within one evaluation fold (the test set comprises five folds of 100,000 chunks; 909–979 chunks per fold for this probe) are ordered by depth into a single sequence that a four-layer Transformer processes jointly, so each prediction can use chunks from all depths of the probe (arcs: schematic self-attention from the CA1 chunk). Both readouts are trained with a Gaussian negative log-likelihood against histology. The chunk predictions (points) are pooled per channel with inverse-variance weights, and the probe's known channel geometry is rigidly fitted to them (Kabsch; no ground-truth coordinates are used); the resulting channel positions (magenta) are compared with histology (black). RMSE values are for this probe and decoder seed 1 (micromanipulator alone: 641 µm; medians over the 118 test probes: 576 µm linear, 818 µm Transformer, 635 µm micromanipulator alone). The probe was chosen for the variety of regions it crosses from the 58 test probes with at least 250 channels, a depth span of at least 2.5 mm and linear fusion better than the micromanipulator alone (rank 14 of 58 by closeness to the median errors). Fig. 3c reports per-probe means over eight seeds.
